REASON
To ensure the development complies with the provisions of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020), and the London Plan (2021).

All existing trees, hedges and landscaping including those shown as retained on the approved plans shall be protected during construction and retained thereafter unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
REASON
To preserve the character of the area in accordance with Policy DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part Two (2020).

The additional rooms hereby approved shall be used solely as part of the existing care home and shall not be used as independent residential accommodation (including any other purpose in Class C2 and not for general needs housing of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987).
REASON

To ensure that the Local Planning Authority retains control over the future use of the building, in order to safeguard the amenities of surrounding residential occupiers, in accordance with Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021).
No development shall commence until a Construction Management Plan (CMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CMP shall include details of:
i. The phasing and programme of development works;
ii. Hours of demolition and construction works;
iii. Measures to control noise, dust and vibration during demolition and construction;
iv. Measures to prevent mud and debris being tracked onto the highway, including wheel-washing facilities;
v. Construction traffic routing, delivery and servicing arrangements, and contractor parking arrangements;
vi. Measures to protect pedestrian and highway safety, including signage and temporary traffic management where required;
vii. Location of site compounds, material storage and loading/unloading areas;
viii. Measures to minimise emissions and impacts on local air quality; and
ix. Details of waste management, recycling and reuse of materials where practicable.

Access to the flat roof over the extension(s) hereby approved shall be for maintenance or emergency purposes only and the flat roof shall not be used as a roof garden, terrace, balcony, patio or similar amenity area.
REASON
To prevent overlooking to adjoining properties in accordance with policy policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building and shall thereafter be retained as such.
REASON

To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and to ensure that the proposed development does not have an adverse effect upon the appearance of the existing building in accordance with Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020)

The Equality Act seeks to protect people accessing goods, facilities and services from discrimination on the basis of a 'protected characteristic', which includes those with a disability. As part of the Act, service providers are obliged to improve access to and within the structure of their building, particularly in situations where reasonable adjustment can be incorporated with relative ease. The Act states that service providers should think ahead to take steps to address barriers that impede disabled people.

Nuisance from demolition and construction works is subject to control under The Control of Pollution Act 1974, the Clean Air Acts and other related legislation. In particular, you should ensure that the following are complied with:-

A. Demolition and construction works which are audible at the site boundary shall only be carried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 hours Monday to Friday and between the hours of 08.00 hours and 13.00 hours on Saturday. No works shall be carried out on Sundays, Bank or Public Holidays.
B. All noise generated during such works shall be controlled in compliance with British Standard Code of Practice BS 5228:2009.
C. Dust emissions shall be controlled in compliance with the Mayor of London's Best Practice Guidance' The Control of dust and emissions from construction and demolition.
D. No bonfires that create dark smoke or nuisance to local residents.

Any damage will require to be made good to the satisfaction of the Council and at the applicant's expense.
